<!-- generated from maestro item 1448 — do not edit; the board item is the source of truth -->
Every project that runs `bin/run_tests` should be able to report its result to maestro automatically, so that a team — or an agent about to start work — can ask whether a project is passing without access to the machine that ran the tests. The runner already builds a complete structured report of every run; what is missing is the identity envelope and the send. Two things must hold: this stays off unless a project explicitly turns it on, because django-mojo is a public framework and a test runner that phones home by default is unacceptable; and a failed send never changes a test run's exit code, because a reporting problem must not look like a test failure.

Scoping added a third rule the original ask did not anticipate: **only a run that is actually the suite's verdict may be pushed.** A `-t module` run, and a `-s` run that stopped at the first failure, both reach the same end-of-run code as a complete run — and maestro answers "is this project green?" from the latest push per suite, so sending either would overwrite the project's real status with a partial one.

Re-filed here 2026-08-06 from the Maestro workspace, where it was mis-filed as a sub-item — framework work is built in this repo, so it belongs on this board.

---

## Spec

Agent-facing from here down. **Kind**: feature · **Requested by**: Ian · **Source**: re-filed from Maestro board item #603 (2026-07-29), which was archived in favour of this one. Framework work routes to NativeMojo per the `maestro-conventions` rule; the original was also parent-nested under a maestro epic, which that rule explicitly forbids for cross-repo dependencies.

### The receiving end is already live

**The maestro half shipped on 2026-08-04**, so this item is unblocked and its contract is settled, not open:

- Endpoint: `POST /api/maestro/testrun`, auth `Authorization: apikey <token>`.
- The wire contract is published as **Test Run Spec v1** — `docs/web_developer/maestro/TestRuns.md` in the maestro repo (`~/Projects/mojo/maestro/api`). Read it; do not re-derive the shape from this workspec.
- Read back with `GET /api/maestro/testrun/status?project=<id>`, or over MCP with `test_status(project)`.
- Related maestro items, by URL (never nest across repos): [#599 Test-run ingest](https://maestromojo.com/workspaces/#/board/8?item=599) (done — the endpoint and record), [#598 Test results epic](https://maestromojo.com/workspaces/#/board/8?item=598) (the parent product direction, in the maestro workspace).

**The naming question the original workspec left open is settled.** Canonical names are `suites` / `suite` / `file`. Maestro additionally accepts testit's raw `--agent` shape via documented ingest aliases (`modules`→`suites`; per-failure `module`→`suite`, `test_file`/`file_path`→`file`) and stores canonical — so a plain `curl` of `var/test_failures.json` plus an envelope already works today. **The reporter should emit canonical names** rather than rely on the alias layer, which exists for hand-rolled pushes.

Three points from the spec that scoping read directly and that shape the plan:

- **`project` is optional and normally omitted** — a project-scoped `apikey` already carries it. It is a configuration convenience, not a requirement, so it must not be part of the enable gate.
- **`null` always reads as "not sent", never as an error.** Only a known field of the *wrong type* is a 400.
- Per-failure string fields cap at 300 chars (`assertion` 500, `traceback` 2000); the suite map keeps 300 entries; bodies over 1 MB are refused.

### Shape

- A `--maestro` flag, or better the existing JSON config — `runner.load_config()` / `apply_config_defaults()` already support one, which is the right home for a URL and a project id.
- Key from the environment, never a config file in the repo. `MAESTRO_API_KEY` is the name the MCP server already uses.
- Envelope fields testit does not currently collect: `project` id, `suite` name, `runner` name/version, `ref` branch/commit, `run_url` under CI, and `version` — the project's OWN version of the code under test (semver, build or deploy tag), which the spec marks SHOULD-report and maestro displays on its status cards. `version` is distinct from `ref.commit` (the VCS identity) and from `runner.version` (testit's own version).
- `schema: "maestro.testrun/1"`.

### The rule this must not break

**A push failure must never fail the test run.** Fire-and-forget with a short timeout. A developer offline, a maestro outage, a bad key, or a timeout produces a warning line and nothing else; the exit code stays a function of the tests alone.

### What already exists in this repo

- `testit/runner.py::_write_agent_report()` (line 1139) builds the complete report — `{status, total, passed, failed, skipped, duration, ran, modules{}, slowest[], failures[], conf_drift[]}` — and writes `var/test_failures.json`. Called once from `main()` at line 1684, guarded by `opts.agent`. It never reads `opts`; the parameter is vestigial. **This builder is ~80% of the item.**
- `setup_parser()` (line 393) holds the flags; `load_config()` (line 319) and `apply_config_defaults()` (line 354) are the JSON-config path, and the **whole** parsed config is kept on `opts.config_data` (line 449) — a nested block needs no `key_map` entry.
- `requests` is already a hard dependency (`pyproject.toml:11`) and testit already uses it (`testit/client.py:1`). No new dependency, which matters because `bin/run_tests` runs `uv run --frozen`.
- `mojo.__version__` (`mojo/__init__.py:1`, currently `1.2.71`) is testit's own version — testit ships inside django-mojo. The **project's** own `version` cannot be inferred generically and comes from config/env.
- `helpers.AGENT_MODE` (set at `main()` line 1389 from `opts.agent`) gates whether per-failure context — `file_path`, `line`, `traceback` — is collected at all (`helpers.py:221,238`).

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Off by default; pushes only when explicitly configured
- [ ] A successful run posts the v1 payload and prints a confirmation
- [ ] An unreachable maestro, a bad key, or a timeout prints a warning and does not change the exit code
- [ ] A failing run still pushes — the red result is the point
- [ ] A **partial** run does not push: `-t`/`--ignore` filtered, or stopped early by `-s` or the abort key, prints one line saying why and posts nothing
- [ ] The key is read from the environment, never persisted in the repo
- [ ] Branch, commit and `run_url` populate under CI and degrade cleanly when absent
- [ ] The project's own `version` is reported when the project makes one available
- [ ] Emitted field names are the canonical `suites` / `suite` / `file`, matching Test Run Spec v1 exactly, and no field is sent carrying a `None` the runner never resolved
- [ ] Docs updated in `docs/django_developer/testit/Overview.md`, stating plainly that assertion messages and tracebacks leave the machine

### Out of scope

- Reporters for other runners (jest, pytest, `go test`) — the contract is public and those are separate work if wanted; anything on the maestro side.
- Usability in maestro's own repo: that needs a django-mojo release and a relock there. Nothing in maestro blocks on this — v1 of the ingest was deliberately built to accept a plain `curl`.

## Plan

### Objective

A configured `bin/run_tests` posts its run to maestro's `/api/maestro/testrun` in the canonical Test Run Spec v1 shape; an unconfigured one does nothing and cannot tell. Only complete, unfiltered runs are pushed. No push outcome — success, refusal, outage, timeout, misconfiguration, or a bug in the reporter itself — ever changes what the runner prints about the tests or the code it exits with.

### Ordered implementation steps

1. **Split the report builder** — `testit/runner.py`. Extract the body of `_write_agent_report()` (lines 1145-1258) into a new `_build_agent_report(opts, display=None, conf_drift=None)` that **returns** the report dict. `_write_agent_report()` becomes: build, write the file, `return report`. Signature and file output unchanged, so the three existing tests that call it (`tests/test_helpers/test_runner_config.py:167,224,266`) keep passing untouched. `_build_agent_report` must stay free of `opts` reads, exactly as the current body is — anything the envelope needs off `opts` is read at the call site in `main()`.

2. **New module `testit/maestro.py`** — all reporter logic, so the 1704-line `runner.py` gains two call sites and nothing else. **No stdlib `logging`, no type hints** (`.claude/rules/core.md`). Prints use the runner's two-space style (`f"\n  Maestro: ..."`). Two public functions, and **both wrap their entire body in `try/except (Exception, KeyboardInterrupt)`** — the runner must not be able to execute any reporter code outside a guard, including the enable check:

   - **`setup(opts)`** → settings `objict` or `None`. Called **early** in `main()` (step 4) so a misconfiguration is reported before a ten-minute suite runs, not after. Returns `None` (reporter off) unless **both**:
     - an explicit enable: `getattr(opts, "maestro", False)` (the `--maestro` flag) **or** a `maestro` block on `getattr(opts, "config_data", None)` that is a **non-empty dict** — `isinstance(block, dict) and block`, so `"maestro": {}` and `"maestro": false` read as "off", which is what anyone writing them means;
     - `url` and a key resolve. **Not `project`** — the spec says a project-scoped key already carries it and it is normally omitted, so requiring it would turn the simplest correct CI setup into a misconfiguration.

     Sources, precedence **env > config block** (there are no CLI flags for the values themselves): `MAESTRO_URL` / `maestro.url`, `MAESTRO_PROJECT` / `maestro.project` (optional; int, and a non-int is a warning rather than a crash), `MAESTRO_SUITE` / `maestro.suite`, `MAESTRO_VERSION` / `maestro.version`, `MAESTRO_TIMEOUT` / `maestro.timeout` (default 5.0), `maestro.diagnostics` (default true — see step 3). The **key is `MAESTRO_API_KEY`, environment only** — never read from the config file, never stored beyond this call, never printed.
     - `--no-maestro` short-circuits to `None` before anything else.
     - Missing `url` while enabled → warn (a misconfiguration).
     - Missing key → warn **only when `--maestro` was passed explicitly**; stay silent when the enable came from a config block, because "CI has the key and my laptop does not" is the expected steady state and must not nag every run.
     - **URL safety, fail-closed**: scheme must be `http` or `https`. `http` is accepted only for a loopback host, decided **without DNS** — `urlparse(url).hostname`, then `h == "localhost"` (exact equality, never `in`/`endswith`, so `localhost.attacker.com` is refused) or `ipaddress.ip_address(h).is_loopback` with a `ValueError` (a name, not an address) treated as not-loopback. The request carries a bearer API key and must not cross a network in cleartext.

   - **`report_run(settings, build_report)`** → bool. Takes the settings from `setup()` and a **zero-argument callable** that builds the report dict, so the build happens inside this guard too. Body: `build_report()` → `build_payload` → `push`. Returns False on any refusal or failure, and raises nothing, ever.

   - Private: `build_payload(report, settings)`, `push(settings, payload)`, `_git_ref()`, `_ci_context()`, `_clean(value, limit)`.

3. **`build_payload(report, settings)`** — envelope plus a translated, trimmed copy. Never mutates `report`; the file on disk and the wire payload are independent.
   - Envelope: `schema` `"maestro.testrun/1"`, `project` (int, **omitted when unset** — the key carries it), `suite` (omitted when unset; maestro defaults it to `"default"`), `source` (`"ci"` when a CI environment is detected, else `"local"`), `version` (omitted when unset), `started` (ISO-8601 UTC ending in `Z`, from `helpers.TEST_RUN.started_at`), `runner` `{"name": "testit", "version": mojo.__version__}`, `ref` (step 5; omitted entirely when empty).
   - Straight through: `status`, `total`, `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `duration`.
   - **Renamed to canonical**: `modules` → `suites`; per failure `module` → `suite`, and `file` = `entry.get("file_path") or entry.get("test_file")` — **`or`, not a membership test**, because `_write_agent_report` assigns `file_path` unconditionally (`runner.py:1160`) and it is frequently `None`, which would shadow a perfectly good `test_file`. Keep `test_name`, `function`, `status`, `assertion`, `line`, `traceback`.
   - **Drop any key whose value is `None`, and confirm a value is a string before capping it.** These fields are `None` in ordinary runs:
     - `assertion` is `record.get("detail")` (`runner.py:1155`) and `detail` is only recorded when truthy (`helpers.py:283`), so a failure whose message is empty yields `None` — and slicing that for the 500-char cap raises `TypeError`, which the outer guard would swallow into "the reporter silently never pushes".
     - `file_path` and `line` are assigned from `agent_ctx.get(...)` (`runner.py:1160-1161`) but only *set* inside a `try` that swallows `OSError, TypeError` (`helpers.py:163-170`) — a decorated or dynamically compiled test leaves both `None`.
     - `module` / `test_file` / `function` come from `_active_context()` (`helpers.py:257-266`) with no fallback and are `None` when no test is active; the same function already defends this at `runner.py:1197` and not at `:1151-1153`.

     Note the reason precisely: the server reads `null` as "not sent" and would **not** 400 on it (Test Run Spec v1, "What maestro is strict about"). The strip exists because capping `None` raises and because a `None` `file_path` must not shadow a real `test_file` — not because the wire rejects nulls.
   - **Dropped, deliberately**: `server_log_tail`, `test_source`, and the top-level `ran`, `slowest`, `conf_drift`. The report file keeps all of them; only the wire copy is trimmed.
   - **`diagnostics: false`** (config) omits the `failures` array entirely — counts, `suites` and envelope only. See the security decision below.
   - Caps, matching the spec's field limits so nothing is sent that cannot be stored: first **50** failures; `traceback` 2000; `assertion` 500; `test_name` / `suite` / `file` / `function` / `status` 300 each; `suites` first **300** entries. Worst case ≈ 150 KB against a 1 MB body cap.
   - No `group` or `group_uuid` key at the top level, by construction.

4. **Wire it into the runner** — `testit/runner.py::main()`, in two places.

   **(a) Early, immediately after `helpers.AGENT_MODE` is set (line 1389):**
   ```
   maestro_settings = testit.maestro.setup(opts)
   helpers.AGENT_MODE = bool(opts.agent) or bool(maestro_settings)
   ```
   Enabling the reporter must imply context collection, or a push carries failures with no `file`, `line` or `traceback` (`helpers.py:221,238`). `opts.agent` still solely controls whether the file is written. Misconfiguration warnings land here, before the suite runs.

   **(b) At the tail (current lines 1674-1699).** The existing `--agent` block at `:1682-1688` is preserved **verbatim**, including the two `print` lines that tell an agent where the report is — the illustrative sketch below omits them only for brevity, and a build session must not delete them:
   ```
   report = _write_agent_report(...) if opts.agent else None   # plus its prints, unchanged
   helpers.TEST_RUN.finished_at = time.time()
   helpers.save_results(...)
   _release_lock()                                             # BEFORE the network call
   if maestro_settings and not _push_refused(opts, aborted):
       testit.maestro.report_run(
           maestro_settings,
           lambda: report if report is not None
                   else _build_agent_report(opts, display=display, conf_drift=drifted))
   if helpers.TEST_RUN.failed > 0:
       sys.exit("  Tests failed!")
   ```
   - After `_release_lock()` so an up-to-5-second HTTP call never holds the single-run lock against a waiting run; before the failure exit so a red run still reports.
   - `display` is in scope (assigned at `:1509`/`:1512`) and already passed at `:1684`.

   **(c) `_push_refused(opts, aborted)`** — a new private helper in `runner.py` returning a reason string or `None`, printed as one line when it refuses:
   - **filtered**: `opts.test_modules` or `opts.ignore_modules` non-empty. A `-t test_helpers` run is 50 tests, not the suite; maestro takes the latest push per `(project, suite)` as the project's status, so pushing it would overwrite a real green with a partial verdict.
   - **aborted**: a new `aborted = False` local in `main()`, set to `True` in every `except helpers.TestitAbort` handler at `:1578, :1605, :1632, :1648, :1658, :1671`, and also when `_abort_event.is_set()`. `TestitAbort` is what `-s` raises on the first failure (`helpers.py:233,250`) and what the rich UI's abort key raises — all of them are caught as `break`/`pass` (`:1295`) and **do** fall through to the tail. `_run_module_in_thread` swallows it at `:1295`, so the event check is what catches the parallel case.
   - `--extra` / `--full` runs are **not** refused: they are complete runs, just of a wider tier. Document that a nightly `--full` stream should use a distinct `suite` name so its larger totals do not alternate with the default tier's.

5. **Ref and CI detection** — private helpers in `testit/maestro.py`.
   - `_ci_context()`: GitHub Actions (`GITHUB_ACTIONS` set) yields `branch` from `GITHUB_REF_NAME`, `commit` from `GITHUB_SHA`, `run_url` from `f"{GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/{GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/{GITHUB_RUN_ID}"` when every part is present. Any truthy `CI` env var alone sets `source` to `"ci"` with no ref.
   - `_git_ref()`: fills what CI did not, via `subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD"], cwd=paths.PROJECT_ROOT, capture_output=True, timeout=2, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)` and the `--abbrev-ref HEAD` variant. `stdin=DEVNULL` so a `git` that decides to prompt can never hang the run. Any non-zero exit, timeout, missing git or non-repository directory → that key is absent. CI values win over git values (a detached-HEAD CI checkout reports `HEAD` as its branch, which is worse than nothing). Verified here: `git -C testproject rev-parse --short HEAD` → `40587cc7`, because `paths.PROJECT_ROOT` (`testproject/`) sits inside the django-mojo worktree.

6. **`push(settings, payload)`** — `requests.post(url, data=json.dumps(payload, default=str), headers={"Authorization": "apikey <key>", "Content-Type": "application/json"}, timeout=settings.timeout, allow_redirects=False)`.
   - **`data=` with an explicit `json.dumps(..., default=str)`, not `json=`.** `requests`' `json=` kwarg serializes with no `default`, so a value the existing file write coerces (`runner.py:1263` uses `default=str` — evidence the author did not trust the types) would raise `TypeError` here and the reporter would silently never push while `test_failures.json` looked perfect.
   - `allow_redirects=False`: a 3xx is a failed push with a warning, never a redirect that could carry the key to another host.
   - 2xx → confirmation line, including `data.failures_truncated` from the reply when true (the spec returns it precisely so a sender knows). Anything else → warn with the status code and at most ~200 characters of the **response** body — the spec puts the reason in an `error` field, so it is worth showing. The key is never printed.

7. **Tests** — new `tests/test_helpers/test_maestro_report.py` (see Testing plan).

8. **Docs** — `docs/django_developer/testit/Overview.md` (see Documentation plan).

### Design decisions

- **A separate `testit/maestro.py`, not more `runner.py`.** runner.py is 1704 lines; the reporter is a self-contained concern with pure, directly testable functions and exactly one impure one.
- **Two ways to turn it on, one AND-gate.** The enable signal must be something that cannot be present by accident: an explicit `--maestro`, or a `maestro` block in the project's own config file. Env vars supply *values* but never enable — deliberately, because `MAESTRO_API_KEY` is the name maestro's MCP server already uses **and** `bin/run_tests` sources the repo's `.env` with `set -a` (lines 19-23), so a developer may well already have it exported into every test run.
- **`project` is not part of the gate.** Test Run Spec v1 says a project-scoped key carries the project and the field is normally omitted; demanding it would make the simplest correct CI setup (URL + key) read as a misconfiguration.
- **Only complete runs push.** maestro's `test_status` treats the latest push per `(project, suite)` as the truth, so a `-t` or aborted run is not merely noisy — it overwrites the project's status with a partial verdict. Refusing costs one printed line; the alternative corrupts the answer the whole feature exists to give.
- **The enable check lives inside the guard.** `setup()` and `report_run()` are both public and both fully wrapped, so the runner's call sites are ordinary statements and no reporter code can run unguarded. `except (Exception, KeyboardInterrupt)` — `KeyboardInterrupt` is not an `Exception`, and the push adds a window where the process sits in a socket call after the tests are already decided; a Ctrl-C there must not replace `sys.exit("  Tests failed!")` with a traceback and exit 130.
- **Settings resolve early, not at the tail.** A misconfiguration warning printed after a ten-minute suite is nearly useless, and enabling the reporter has to imply `AGENT_MODE` before any test runs or the failures carry no context.
- **No default URL, ever.** django-mojo is a public framework; hardcoding a maestromojo.com endpoint into it, even unused, is the wrong shape.
- **Cleartext refused off-loopback**, decided without a DNS lookup. The request carries a bearer API key; the repo's security rule is fail-closed.
- **Honesty about what is sent, plus a switch.** Dropping `server_log_tail` and `test_source` is worth doing, but it does **not** make the payload safe: `assert_eq` interpolates the actual and expected values into the message (`helpers.py:542`, and `assert_in` at `:548` interpolates the whole container), and this repo has tests that assert on secrets by construction — `tests/test_register/passwordless.py:242` on an `access_token`, `tests/test_models/return_real_error.py:72` on `SECRET_TEXT`. Tracebacks (`helpers.py:174`, errors only) carry source lines. So: say it plainly in the docs rather than implying the trim made it safe, and give `maestro.diagnostics: false` for a project that wants green/red without assertion text leaving the box. Sending them by default is right — "the red result is the point" — but as stated consent, not a surprise.
- **Synchronous push with a timeout, and an honest claim about it.** A thread whose lifetime races `sys.exit` is not worth it. But `timeout=` bounds each socket operation, not wall clock: `getaddrinfo` runs before it applies, and a read timeout is per-chunk. Document that a wedged resolver can exceed it, rather than promising five seconds the code cannot deliver.
- **Nothing is added to `key_map`.** `opts.config_data` already carries the whole parsed config (`runner.py:449`), and these settings are a nested block.

### Edge cases and error handling

- Reporter unconfigured (the overwhelming majority of runs, including every run of django-mojo's own suite by default) → `setup()` returns `None` before any work; nothing is built, no network is touched, nothing is printed.
- `--maestro` with nothing configured → one warning naming what is missing, printed **before** the suite runs.
- Config block present, `MAESTRO_API_KEY` absent → silent skip (the laptop case).
- `MAESTRO_PROJECT` non-integer → one warning; the push still goes, without `project`, because the key carries it.
- Non-http(s) scheme, or `http://` to a non-loopback host → one warning, no push.
- `-t` / `--ignore` filtered run, or a run aborted by `-s` or the abort key → one line saying the run was partial, no push. **This includes the common `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_helpers` iteration loop.**
- maestro unreachable, DNS failure, TLS failure, timeout → one warning; exit code still a pure function of the tests.
- 401/403 (bad or foreign key) → warning with the status code; the key is never printed. 3xx → treated as a failure, not followed. 400 → warning carrying the server's `error` text, truncated.
- Ctrl-C during the push → swallowed; the run's own verdict and exit code stand.
- A red run → pushes, and the confirmation says so.
- A non-`--agent` push still carries `file`/`line`/`traceback`, because step 4(a) turns `AGENT_MODE` on whenever the reporter is enabled.
- `display=None` (any `--plain`, `-v`, `-s`, or `-j 1` run) takes the fallback module branch at `runner.py:1194-1207`, whose entries carry **no `duration`** unlike the tracker branch at `:1181-1193`. Absent is fine — every `suites` sub-field is optional.
- A run with zero recorded modules → `total: 0, status: "passed"`; still posts, which is what the spec's four-field minimum accepts.
- `git` absent or `PROJECT_ROOT` outside a work tree → `ref` keys omitted; `ref` dropped entirely when it would be empty.
- A `KeyboardInterrupt` in plain mode that escapes `main()` entirely never reaches the tail — no push, and (pre-existing behavior, not this item's to fix) the run lock is left behind.

### Testing plan

New module `tests/test_helpers/test_maestro_report.py` — pure in-process tests, no database and no dev-server traffic, so `@th.unit_test` except where Django is needed. Every test saves and restores the `MAESTRO_*`/`GITHUB_*`/`CI` environment entries in a `finally`, the discipline `test_runner_config.py:352-357` uses for `paths` globals. Every assert carries a failure message (`.claude/rules/testing.md`).

- **Off by default** — no flag, no config block, `MAESTRO_URL`/`MAESTRO_PROJECT`/`MAESTRO_API_KEY` all exported → `setup()` returns `None`. This pins "cannot phone home by accident", and it is the test that matters most in a public framework.
- **`--no-maestro` wins** over both a config block and `--maestro`.
- **Enable paths** — `--maestro` + env values; config block + env key; env overrides config values; **url + key with no project enables** (the normal CI shape); `"maestro": {}` and `"maestro": false` do **not** enable.
- **Missing pieces** — no url → `None`; no key with a config-block enable → `None`, nothing printed; no key with `--maestro` → `None` plus a warning (capture stdout).
- **URL safety** — `ftp://`, `file://`, `http://maestro.example.com` and `http://localhost.attacker.com` refused; `http://127.0.0.1:8000`, `http://localhost:8000` and `https://…` accepted.
- **Canonical names** — feed `build_payload` a report shaped exactly like `_build_agent_report`'s output: `suites` present, `modules` absent; failures carry `suite` and `file`, never `module`/`test_file`.
- **None handling (regression-grade)** — a failure entry with `assertion: None`, `file_path: None`, `line: None`, `module: None` (the real shapes documented in step 3) must produce a payload with those keys **absent**, and `build_payload` must not raise. Plus `file_path: None` with a real `test_file` → `file` takes the `test_file` value, proving `or` rather than a membership test.
- **Trimming** — `server_log_tail`, `test_source`, `ran`, `slowest`, `conf_drift` absent; the input report dict is unmodified after the call; `diagnostics: false` omits `failures` while keeping counts and `suites`.
- **Caps** — 60 failures → 50; a 5000-char traceback → 2000; a 900-char `test_name` → 300; 400 suites → 300.
- **Envelope** — `schema`, `runner.version == mojo.__version__`, `started` ISO-8601 ending in `Z`, `project` absent when unset and present when set, `source` `"ci"` under a faked `GITHUB_ACTIONS`/`CI` and `"local"` without, `ref.run_url` assembled from the Actions variables, `version` present only when configured, and no `group`/`group_uuid` at the top level.
- **Serialization** — a payload carrying a non-JSON-native value (e.g. a `Path`) serializes through `json.dumps(..., default=str)` rather than raising, pinning the `data=`-not-`json=` decision.
- **Partial-run refusal** — `_push_refused` returns a reason for `opts.test_modules` non-empty, for `opts.ignore_modules` non-empty, and for `aborted=True`; returns `None` for a clean unfiltered run and for one carrying `--extra`/`--full`.
- **Failure isolation** (the item's central rule) — with `requests.post` monkeypatched in turn to raise `ConnectionError`, raise `Timeout`, raise `KeyboardInterrupt`, return 500, return 401 and return 302, `report_run` returns falsy, prints one warning, and **raises nothing**. Plus one test where the `build_report` callable itself raises, and one where `setup()` is fed a config object that raises on attribute access — proving the outer guards, not just the inner ones.
- **Success path** — a fake `post` returning 200 → truthy, confirmation printed, and the captured request carries `Authorization: apikey …`, `Content-Type: application/json`, and a body that round-trips through `json.loads`.

Not tested here, deliberately: a live push to maestro (below, as manual evidence), and `_build_agent_report`'s content, which the three existing tests in `test_runner_config.py` already cover and which this change must leave untouched.

### Documentation plan

- `docs/django_developer/testit/Overview.md`:
  - New `### Maestro Reporting` subsection immediately after `### Agent Mode` (line 137-148): what it does; that it is off unless configured and cannot be enabled by environment variables alone; the two enable paths; the settings table (env name / config key / default); `MAESTRO_API_KEY`-from-environment-only; that `project` is optional because the key carries it; the cleartext refusal; the "a push never changes the exit code" guarantee **and its honest limit** (the timeout bounds socket operations, not wall clock); that partial runs (`-t`, `--ignore`, `-s`, aborted) do not push and why; and — stated plainly, not buried — **that failing assertion messages and error tracebacks are sent to the configured server**, what that can contain, and that `maestro.diagnostics: false` turns it off.
  - `### JSON Config` (line 195-220): add the `maestro` block to the example and key list, noting it is a nested object rather than a flat default.
  - Link the wire contract to maestro's published Test Run Spec v1 by URL rather than restating it — one copy of a contract, and it is not this repo's.
- **No `docs/web_developer/` change.** That track documents REST endpoints this framework *serves*; this is dev tooling that calls someone else's documented endpoint. Recorded here so the omission reads as a decision, not an oversight.
- **No `CHANGELOG.md`** (`.claude/rules/docs.md`) — the board item is the changelog.

### Verification

- **Tier:** full
- **Run:** baseline `bin/run_tests --agent` before the first edit, recording totals and any pre-existing failures from `testproject/var/test_failures.json`; the whole suite `bin/run_tests --agent` again after implementing; `bin/run_tests --agent -t test_helpers` while iterating.
- **Why:** the change edits `testit/` — which `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md` names explicitly as a full-tier trigger — and specifically the runner's end-of-run path, the `AGENT_MODE` assignment every module's failure context depends on, and the `_write_agent_report` refactor. A defect here does not fail one module; it breaks the harness that reports all of them.
- **Read the report by eye after the closing run.** A broken report writer produces a plausible file, not an error, so the post-change comparison is self-referential unless someone opens `testproject/var/test_failures.json` and confirms its shape.
- **Manual evidence (recommended, not blocking):** one live push against maestro's deployed `/api/maestro/testrun` with a scratch `apikey` minted on the django-mojo project group, then the row read back via `test_status(12)`. It is the only proof the emitted names satisfy the real validator rather than this repo's reading of the spec. The key stays in the environment and never lands in the repo.

### Challenge

Independent red-team (fresh-context agent, read-only repo access); every objection re-verified against the source by the scoping session before disposition.

| # | Objection | Disposition | Evidence / what changed |
|---|-----------|-------------|-------------------------|
| 1 | "An aborted run never reaches the tail" is false — `TestitAbort` is caught as `break`, and `-s` raises it on the first failure, so a stop-on-fail run would push a partial suite as the project's status | **amended** | Verified `runner.py:1578,1605,1632,1648,1658,1671` (caught as `break`), `:1295` (swallowed in the thread), `helpers.py:233,250` (raised by `STOP_ON_FAIL`). Added `_push_refused` + an `aborted` flag; the false claim is gone. |
| 2 | Per-failure `assertion`, `file_path`, `line`, `module` are routinely `None`; capping `None` raises `TypeError` and silently kills every push | **amended (with one correction to the objection)** | The `None` values are real — verified `runner.py:1155,1160-1161`, `helpers.py:283,163-170,257-266`. The challenger's added claim that `null` risks a 400 is **wrong**: Test Run Spec v1 states `null` reads as "not sent". The strip is kept for the `TypeError` and for `file_path` shadowing `test_file`, and the plan states that narrower reason. |
| 3 | The runner had no guarded way to ask "is the reporter on?" — the enable check sat outside the one try/except the whole guarantee rests on, and would double-print warnings | **amended** | API is now `setup(opts)` + `report_run(settings, build_report)`, both public, both fully guarded; the build is a callable evaluated inside the guard. |
| 4 | Dropping `server_log_tail` does not make the payload safe — `assert_eq`/`assert_in` interpolate actual values, and this repo asserts on secrets by construction | **amended** | Verified `helpers.py:542,548,552`; `tests/test_register/passwordless.py:242` (access_token), `tests/test_models/return_real_error.py:72` (SECRET_TEXT). Docs now state it plainly; added `maestro.diagnostics: false`. Default stays on — "the red result is the point" — but as stated consent. |
| 5 | A `-t module` run pushes as if it were the whole suite, and maestro's latest-push-wins makes that overwrite the project's real status | **amended** | Verified filtered runs reach the same tail; `.claude/rules/build-baseline.md` treats scoped/whole/`--full` as three different things. `_push_refused` refuses filtered runs; `--extra`/`--full` still push, with a docs note to give a wider tier its own `suite` name. |
| 6 | `requests`' `json=` kwarg has no `default=str`, so a type the existing file write coerces would `TypeError` and the reporter would silently never push | **amended** | Verified `runner.py:1263` writes with `default=str`. Switched to `data=json.dumps(payload, default=str)` + explicit `Content-Type`, with a test. |
| 7 | `except Exception` misses `KeyboardInterrupt`; `timeout=` does not bound wall clock (getaddrinfo, per-chunk reads); `subprocess` inherits stdin | **amended** | Correct on all three. Guards now catch `(Exception, KeyboardInterrupt)`; `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` added; the docs state the timeout's real bound instead of promising five seconds. |
| 8 | Building the report without `--agent` yields failures with no `file`/`line`/`traceback`, because context collection is gated on `AGENT_MODE` | **amended** | Verified `helpers.py:221,238`, `runner.py:1389`. Enabling the reporter now implies `AGENT_MODE`, resolved early in `main()` — which also moves misconfiguration warnings to before the suite instead of after it. |
| 9 | The step-4 snippet silently dropped the two `--agent` prints that tell an agent where the report is | **amended** | Verified `runner.py:1685-1688`. Snippet marked illustrative; preserving those lines is now an explicit instruction. |
| 10 | `"maestro" in config` would enable on `{}` or `false`; `opts.maestro` attribute access breaks for hand-built opts (as the plan's own tests use) | **amended** | `isinstance(block, dict) and block`, `getattr(opts, ...)` throughout, plus `MAESTRO_TIMEOUT` for consistency with every other setting. |

**Post-challenge correction from the published spec** (read directly at `~/Projects/mojo/maestro/api/docs/web_developer/maestro/TestRuns.md`, which this workspec instructs): the draft plan required `project` to enable the reporter. The spec says a project-scoped key carries the project and the field is **normally omitted**, so `project` was dropped from the enable gate and is now an optional envelope field. Per-failure string caps were also aligned to the spec's 300-char limits. Neither is a challenge finding; both are the workspec's own instruction being followed.

The challenger separately verified and raised **no objection** to: `display` being in scope at the tail (`:1509,1512`); the `_write_agent_report` split leaving the three existing tests passing (it never reads `opts`); `opts.config_data` being populated unconditionally (`:449`); env-alone-cannot-enable holding up even though `bin/run_tests` sources `.env` with `set -a`; no new dependency under `uv run --frozen`; `--list-extras` and lock contention being the only non-abort early exits; the loopback check being decidable without DNS; the cap arithmetic (≈150 KB against 1 MB); `paths.PROJECT_ROOT` as the git cwd; `group`/`group_uuid` being top-level-only and unable to collide with nested module names; and the `full` verification tier.
